description: How a Snowflake semantic view is read. `SHOW SEMANTIC VIEWS` lists the views a selection reaches, and `SYSTEM$READ_YAML_FROM_SEMANTIC_VIEW` returns each one's specification as YAML. What the reader takes from that YAML is what the model is offered: the public members it can query, the variables it must bind, the tables the view depends on, and the prose that becomes first-touch and retrieval context. Both packages read the same YAML into the same model, so an agent sees the same view whichever package built it.

show_rows.description: Rows of `SHOW SEMANTIC VIEWS` and the views they list. Drivers report the column names in either case, every column but the name, namespace, and comment is ignored, and a blank or null comment is no description.

cases.name: lower-case keys, and a blank comment is no description
upper-case keys, and a null comment
no rows

specifications.description: A view's id, its YAML specification exactly as Snowflake returns it, and the model read from it. `description` is the comment `SHOW SEMANTIC VIEWS` reported, used when the YAML has none. Entries may be a list or a mapping keyed by name. Members marked private are dropped, `labels` containing `filter` (in any case) marks a dimension or fact usable as a named filter, and a member's type is its `data_type`. A base table's database, schema, and table are SQL identifiers: a quoted one is exact, with doubled quotes undone, an unquoted one is upper-cased, and a missing database or schema is the view's own. `identity`, when given, is the view's warehouse id and `id` the label a caller named it by; the view's own namespace comes from `identity`. Dependencies are complete only when every table names one and there is at least one. `expected` is either the model, or `unsupported` with the reason when a variable cannot be bound: its type is missing or not bindable, its name is declared twice, or its default is null or is not a literal of its type.

name: ORDERS_PARAM_MODEL
description: "Orders, with a threshold variable."
variables:
  - name: MIN_TOTAL
    description: Only orders whose total is at least this amount count.
    data_type: "NUMBER(10,2)"
    default_value: "0"
tables:
  - name: ORDERS
    base_table:
      database: ANALYTICS
      schema: PUBLIC
      table: '"orders"'
    facts:
      - name: ORDER_TOTAL
        expr: '"order_total"'
        data_type: FLOAT
        access_modifier: public_access
    metrics:
      - name: TOTAL_ABOVE_MIN
        description: Sum of order totals at or above MIN_TOTAL.
        expr: SUM(orders.order_total)
        access_modifier: public_access

sql_types.description: A variable's declared type and the SQL type its bound value is cast to, or null when the declared text is not safe to splice into SQL: letters and underscores, optionally followed by a precision and scale.

metric_sql.description: The `SEMANTIC_VIEW` query a call over native metrics compiles to. Names resolve against the model's members as `semantic-models.json` pins. Members are referenced by logical table and name, named filters become bare conditions, and each `where` entry becomes a comparison on a dimension: a value matching an optional minus, digits, and an optional fraction is written bare unless the entry sets `quoted`, and anything else is a string literal, with each backslash and single quote doubled because Snowflake reads a backslash in a literal as an escape. Each `arguments` name is bound as `?`, cast to the type the view declares when that type is safe to splice. An error is pinned by the names its message must mention. Its `error` field names the kind of failure for a reader, and neither suite asserts it.

selection.description: Which semantic views a `tables` selection reads up front, which it leaves as stubs, and which relations remain tables. A view an entry names exactly is read up front and keeps the label it was named by, and one that cannot be used fails the selection. A namespace's views are stubs, read only when inspected or used, so one that cannot be used is found out then. A view over exactly named relations is read up front when those relations include every table it reads, and is skipped quietly when it cannot be read or used, or when a table it reads names no table. `exclude` drops views by name, and a listing that fails lists no views. Views count toward the object limit with relations, as `catalog-merge.json` sets it; a case's `object_limit` lowers it, and the views listed beside an exact relation count before any is read. `reads`, when given, names the views whose YAML the selection read, in order. A `tables` entry is a string, or an object naming a namespace by its `catalog` and `schema`. `warehouse` is the catalog every case reads, all in ANALYTICS.PUBLIC, whose current namespace it is.

semantic_views.REVENUE_MODEL:
name: revenue
tables:
  - name: orders
    base_table: {database: ANALYTICS, schema: PUBLIC, table: ORDERS}
    metrics:
      - name: revenue
semantic_views.ACROSS_MODEL:
tables:
  - name: orders
    base_table: {database: ANALYTICS, schema: PUBLIC, table: ORDERS}
    metrics:
      - name: revenue
  - name: sales
    base_table: {database: ANALYTICS, schema: PUBLIC, table: SALES}
semantic_views.PAYLOAD_MODEL:
variables:
  - name: payload
    data_type: VARIANT
tables:
  - name: orders
    base_table: {database: ANALYTICS, schema: PUBLIC, table: ORDERS}
    metrics:
      - name: revenue
semantic_views.PARTIAL_MODEL:
tables:
  - name: orders
    base_table: {database: ANALYTICS, schema: PUBLIC, table: ORDERS}
    metrics:
      - name: revenue
  - name: other
    base_table: {database: ANALYTICS, schema: PUBLIC}
semantic_views.EMPTY_MODEL:
tables:
  - name: hidden
    base_table: {database: ANALYTICS, schema: PUBLIC, table: HIDDEN}
    metrics:
      - name: secret
        access_modifier: private_access

hydration.description: When a model listed by a namespace selection is read. Every case starts from a fresh source over `selection.warehouse` with `tables` unset, so every view is listed and none is read, and runs its steps in order on that one source, as two agents sharing it would. A `call_metrics` step reads the listed models its `MODEL::member` names point at and keeps them, so a later step does not read them again; an unqualified name reads nothing. A `describe` step reads a listed model each time without keeping it. A step with `error` must fail, mentioning each of its `mentions`. `reads` names the views read, in order, and `models` the labels kept as read once every step has run.

verified_queries.description: The exact trusted queries a view's `verified_queries` declare, read as calculations the agent can run unchanged. A query's description is its `question`, or its name when it has none. A query without a name or SQL, a question that is not text, a repeated name, SQL that is not one read-only SELECT or WITH, and a `{{placeholder}}` (verified queries take no arguments) each make the view unreadable. Errors are pinned as the phrases the message must contain; a case with no phrases pins only the refusal, because each language words that error its own way.

cases.name: a question describes its query, as Snowflake returns them
cases.yaml:
verified_queries:
  - name: TOTAL_ORDER_VALUE_BY_TILE
    sql: "SELECT \"tile_size\", SUM(\"order_total\") AS total FROM \"ANALYTICS\".\"PUBLIC\".\"orders\" GROUP BY \"tile_size\""
    question: What is the total order value for each tile size?
    use_as_onboarding_question: false

calculation_runs.description: The SQL `call_calculation` sends to the warehouse for a verified query: the query exactly as the view declares it. Every case lists one view, `REVENUE_MODEL` in ANALYTICS.PUBLIC with the case's `yaml`, beside the relation ORDERS, and calls `calculation` on a source over that listing, so the call reads the view first. `sent` is the last statement the warehouse receives.
